sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to level up from simple lists? Multidimensional arrays let you organize data in grids, cubes, and beyond!

• What multidimensional arrays are and why they’re useful
• How to create and use 2D arrays (like spreadsheets!)
• Real-world examples where they shine

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine a **chessboard**. It’s not just a list of squares - it’s a grid with rows and columns. That’s exactly what a 2D array is!

Think of it like:
- A **spreadsheet** (rows × columns)
- A **game board** (like tic-tac-toe)
- A **pixel grid** in an image

In Java, a 2D array is simply an array of arrays. Here’s the magic:

**Declaring a 2D array** is easy:
```java
int[][] grid = new int[3][3]; // 3 rows, 3 columns
```

• First `[]` = rows (like floors in a building)
• Second `[]` = columns (like rooms on each floor)
• You can have 3D, 4D... but 2D is most common!

**Accessing elements** works like coordinates:
```java
grid[1][2] = 5; // Row 1, Column 2 gets value 5
```

• Remember: **indexes start at 0** (like most arrays)
• `grid.length` = number of rows
• `grid[0].length` = number of columns in first row

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ 2D arrays = arrays of arrays (like a grid)
✓ Great for tables, game boards, and matrices!

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use nested loops to process 2D arrays (row by row)
donts: Assume all rows have the same length (jagged arrays exist!)
sections.protip: For game boards, use `final int SIZE = 8;` to easily change dimensions later!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where you’ll see multidimensional arrays in action:

examples.how: Pixels are stored in 2D arrays (RGB values for each pixel)
Chess, Sudoku, and tic-tac-toe use 2D arrays to track moves
Matrices (2D arrays) store measurements like temperature grids
Excel-like programs use 2D arrays to store cell values

problem.description:
Create a 3×3 tic-tac-toe board. Write a method `printBoard(char[][] board)` that prints it like this:

X | O | X
---------
O | X | O
---------
  | X |
hints: Use nested loops to iterate through rows and columns
Print "---------" after every row except the last one
Check if a cell is empty (' ') before printing
problem.explanation: The solution uses nested loops to print each row. The inner loop prints each cell with " | " separators, while the outer loop adds the "---------" line between rows.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Multidimensional arrays organize data in grids (2D), cubes (3D), etc.
📌 Practice with nested loops to process them efficiently
📌 Ready for next topic: Processing 2D arrays like a pro!
